# Platform Observability Registry

<!-- Generated from src/fastapicommon/metrics/registry.json by `make metrics-inventory`. Do not edit. -->

Every metric carries the centrally injected const labels `domain`, `service`, `environment`. Required labels: platform tier `domain`, `service`, `environment`, domain tier `service`, `environment`, service tier `service`, `environment`.

## Tier 1: platform-shared metrics

| Metric | Owner | Type | Status | Labels | Meaning | Aggregation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `platform_build_info` | platform-gincommon | gauge | proposed | `version` | Always 1; the version label carries the build of the emitting service. | count by (domain, environment, version) for rollout tracking; never summed. |
| `platform_http_requests_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `method`, `route`, `status_class`, `error_class` | HTTP requests completed by the server, including recovered panics (counted as 5xx). | sum by (domain, service, environment, ...) of rate(); safe to sum across services and domains. |
| `platform_http_request_duration_seconds` | platform-gincommon | histogram (request_duration) | proposed | `method`, `route`, `status_class`, `error_class` | HTTP server request latency in seconds, measured by MetricsMiddleware. | histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket); buckets are identical in every service. |
| `platform_http_request_size_bytes` | platform-gincommon | histogram (payload_size) | proposed | `method`, `route`, `status_class`, `error_class` | HTTP request body size in bytes from Content-Length (not observed when the length is unknown, e.g. chunked uploads). | histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket). |
| `platform_http_response_size_bytes` | platform-gincommon | histogram (payload_size) | proposed | `method`, `route`, `status_class`, `error_class` | HTTP response body size in bytes. | histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket). |
| `platform_http_active_requests` | platform-gincommon | gauge | proposed | `route` | HTTP requests currently being handled. | sum by (domain, service, environment); also an HPA signal. |
| `platform_http_panics_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `method`, `route` | HTTP handler panics recovered by the middleware stack. | sum by (domain, service, environment) of increase(). |
| `platform_http_rate_limited_requests_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `method`, `route` | HTTP requests answered with 429 Too Many Requests. | sum by (domain, service, environment, route) of rate(). |
| `platform_http_request_timeouts_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `method`, `route` | HTTP requests whose TimeoutMiddleware deadline expired before the handler responded. | sum by (domain, service, environment, route) of rate(). |
| `platform_grpc_server_handled_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `grpc_method`, `grpc_code`, `status_class`, `error_class` | gRPC server RPCs completed, including recovered panics (counted as Internal). | sum by (domain, service, environment, ...) of rate(); safe to sum across services and domains. |
| `platform_grpc_server_handling_seconds` | platform-gincommon | histogram (request_duration) | proposed | `grpc_method`, `status_class`, `error_class` | gRPC server RPC latency in seconds. | histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket); buckets are identical in every service. |
| `platform_grpc_server_request_size_bytes` | platform-gincommon | histogram (payload_size) | proposed | `grpc_method`, `status_class`, `error_class` | gRPC request message size in bytes (sum over messages for streams). | histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket). |
| `platform_grpc_server_response_size_bytes` | platform-gincommon | histogram (payload_size) | proposed | `grpc_method`, `status_class`, `error_class` | gRPC response message size in bytes (sum over messages for streams). | histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket). |
| `platform_grpc_server_inflight_requests` | platform-gincommon | gauge | proposed | `grpc_method` | gRPC server RPCs currently being handled. | sum by (domain, service, environment); also an HPA signal. |
| `platform_grpc_rate_limited_requests_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `grpc_method` | gRPC RPCs that ended with ResourceExhausted. | sum by (domain, service, environment, grpc_method) of rate(). |
| `platform_grpc_panics_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `grpc_method` | gRPC handler panics recovered by the interceptor stack. | sum by (domain, service, environment) of increase(). |
| `platform_unclassified_errors_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | approved | `transport` | Errors that reached the top-level error handler unclassified and were answered as a generic internal error (HTTP 500 internal-error, gRPC Internal): a programming defect. | Alert on any: sum by (domain, service, environment) (increase(platform_unclassified_errors_total[5m])) > 0. Trend: sum by (domain, service, transport) (rate(platform_unclassified_errors_total[1h])). |
| `platform_messages_received_total` | platform-events | counter | approved | `queue` | A message delivered to a consumer by its queue (one per SQS delivery, redeliveries included), counted on receipt before it is parsed. | Inbound rate per service: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_received_total[5m])). Platform-wide: sum by (domain) (…). |
| `platform_messages_processed_total` | platform-events | counter | approved | `queue`, `event_type` | A received message whose handler completed successfully, after which the message was acknowledged (deleted). Messages dead-lettered instead are counted in platform_dlq_messages_total, not here. | Success ratio: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_processed_total[5m])) / sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_received_total[5m])). |
| `platform_messages_failed_total` | platform-events | counter | approved | `queue`, `event_type`, `reason` | A received message that could not be processed on this delivery, by reason: malformed (not a valid envelope), decode_error (schema-registry codec failure), handler_error, handler_panic, or dead_letter_error (dead-letter handling or DLQ forwarding failed). A failed message is retried or dead-lettered; see platform_retry_total and platform_dlq_messages_total. | Failure ratio: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_failed_total[5m])) / sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_received_total[5m])). Poison producers: sum by (domain, service, queue) (rate(platform_messages_failed_total{reason="malformed"}[15m])). |
| `platform_retry_total` | platform-events | counter | approved | `operation`, `event_type` | An attempt that failed and was left for automatic retry: a consumed message whose processing failed and stays on its queue for redelivery (operation=consume), or an outbox publish that failed with attempts remaining (operation=outbox_publish). | Retry pressure per service: sum by (domain, service, operation) (rate(platform_retry_total[5m])). |
| `platform_dlq_messages_total` | platform-events | counter | approved | `operation`, `event_type`, `reason` | A message moved to dead-letter storage: forwarded to its SQS queue's RedrivePolicy DLQ (operation=consume), or moved to outbox_dead_letters after exhausting its publish attempts (operation=outbox_publish), by reason. | Dead-letter inflow: sum by (domain, service, operation, reason) (increase(platform_dlq_messages_total[15m])). Any sustained non-zero rate needs attention. |
| `platform_duplicate_messages_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `queue`, `event_type` | A redelivered message acknowledged without running its handler because the consumer's dedup ledger (inbox processed_events) had already recorded its event ID. | Duplicate ratio: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_duplicate_messages_total[15m])) / sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_received_total[15m])). |
| `platform_dependency_request_seconds` | platform-events | histogram (dependency_request) | proposed | `dependency`, `operation`, `outcome` | Client-observed wall time of one call to an external dependency — SNS (publish, publish_batch), SQS (receive_message, delete_message, change_message_visibility, send_message, get_queue_attributes, get_queue_url) or the configured schema-registry codec (encode, decode) — by outcome. The _count series counts calls. receive_message is a long poll: its duration includes up to WaitTimeSeconds (default 20 s) of waiting on an empty queue, so exclude it from latency views (it stays meaningful for error rates). | Error ratio: sum by (domain, service, dependency) (rate(platform_dependency_request_seconds_count{outcome="error"}[5m])) / sum by (domain, service, dependency) (rate(platform_dependency_request_seconds_count[5m])). p99 (long-poll receives excluded): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, domain, service, dependency, operation) (rate(platform_dependency_request_seconds_bucket{operation!="receive_message"}[5m]))). |
| `platform_event_propagation_seconds` | platform-events | histogram (event_propagation) | proposed | `queue`, `event_type` | Time from an event's creation (envelope `time`, set by the producer) to its FIRST receipt by a consumer (ApproximateReceiveCount ≤ 1) — end-to-end propagation delay through the outbox, SNS and SQS. Redeliveries are not observed, so retry delay does not inflate it. Negative clock skew is clamped to 0. | p95 propagation per consumer: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, domain, service, queue) (rate(platform_event_propagation_seconds_bucket[5m]))). Includes producer clock skew. |
| `platform_queue_depth` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | `queue` | Messages waiting on a consumer's queue to be received (SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages — visible, not in flight or delayed), sampled by the consumer every WithQueueDepthMetrics interval. Approximate by SQS design. | Every replica samples the same queue, so aggregate with max, not sum: max by (domain, service, queue) (platform_queue_depth). The natural HPA/KEDA scaling signal once ratified. |
| `platform_dlq_depth` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | `queue` | Messages sitting in the dead-letter queue attached to a consumer's queue by its RedrivePolicy (SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages of the DLQ), sampled with platform_queue_depth. queue is the SOURCE queue's name, so the gauge joins with the consumer's other queue metrics. | max by (domain, service, queue) (platform_dlq_depth) > 0 — messages awaiting investigation or replay. Complements platform_dlq_messages_total (inflow) with the backlog. |
| `platform_messages_in_flight` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | `queue` | Messages a consumer has received and is currently processing (decode, dead-letter routing or handler), per replica. At the consumer's concurrency limit for long periods means the replica is saturated; a value that never drops points at a hung handler (see WithHandlerTimeout). | sum by (domain, service, queue) (platform_messages_in_flight) for total work in progress; compare per replica against the configured concurrency for saturation. |
| `platform_messages_published_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `topic`, `event_type`, `outcome`<br>`outcome` ∈ `success`, `error` | One event a producer attempted to publish to a topic, by outcome (error includes validation, encoding and broker failures; a batch counts each message). | Publish error ratio: sum by (domain, service, topic) (rate(platform_messages_published_total{outcome="error"}[5m])) / sum by (domain, service, topic) (rate(platform_messages_published_total[5m])). |
| `platform_message_processing_duration_seconds` | platform-events | histogram (message_processing) | proposed | `queue`, `event_type` | Wall time a consumer's handler (or dead-letter handler) spent on one delivery, whatever the outcome. | p99 handler latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, domain, service, queue) (rate(platform_message_processing_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))). |
| `platform_outbox_pending_events` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | - | Events in a service's transactional outbox that are due to be published (unpublished, not leased and not waiting out a retry backoff), sampled every outbox GaugeInterval (default 15s) and capped at 100000 (a reading of 100000 means at least that many). Left at its last value when the count query fails (see platform_outbox_errors_total{operation="pending_count"}). | Backlog per service: max by (domain, service) (platform_outbox_pending_events) — every runner reads the same table, so use max, not sum. |
| `platform_outbox_leased_events` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | - | Unpublished outbox events not yet due: claimed by a runner and being published, or waiting out a retry backoff. Sampled every GaugeInterval, capped at 100000. | max by (domain, service) (platform_outbox_leased_events). |
| `platform_outbox_oldest_pending_age` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | - | Age of the oldest unpublished outbox event (now − created_at), 0 when nothing is unpublished, sampled every GaugeInterval. Transient publish failures never dead-letter, so this is the signal that delivery has stopped even when the backlog is small (e.g. a credential outage on a low-volume service). | max by (domain, service) (platform_outbox_oldest_pending_age) — every runner reads the same table. Alert on it staying above the delivery-latency objective (e.g. > 600 for 10m) once ratified. |
| `platform_outbox_ordering_blocked_events` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | - | Ordered outbox events (outbox.EnqueueOrdered) waiting behind an earlier unpublished record with the same ordering key. Sampled every GaugeInterval, capped at 100000. A value that keeps growing means a key's head record keeps failing and holds the rest of its key. | max by (domain, service) (platform_outbox_ordering_blocked_events) — every runner reads the same table. |
| `platform_message_timeouts_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `queue`, `event_type`, `operation`<br>`operation` ∈ `decode`, `dead_letter_handler`, `handler` | A received message whose WithHandlerTimeout deadline expired, by the stage it expired in: decode (codec decode), dead_letter_handler, or handler. Each is also counted in platform_messages_failed_total under its usual reason (decode_error, dead_letter_error, handler_error) — this counter separates timeouts from other failures without changing that Canonical metric's vocabulary. | Timeout share of failures: sum by (domain, service, queue) (rate(platform_message_timeouts_total[5m])) / sum by (domain, service, queue) (rate(platform_messages_failed_total[5m])). |
| `platform_outbox_publish_attempts_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `event_type`, `outcome`<br>`outcome` ∈ `success`, `error` | One attempt by the outbox runner to publish a claimed outbox event, by outcome. | Outbox publish error ratio: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_outbox_publish_attempts_total{outcome="error"}[5m])) / sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_outbox_publish_attempts_total[5m])). |
| `platform_outbox_errors_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `operation`<br>`operation` ∈ `poll`, `unmarshal`, `mark_published`, `pending_count`, `leased_count`, `oldest_pending`, `blocked_count` | An outbox runner step that failed outside a publish attempt: poll (claiming a batch), unmarshal (a stored envelope that no longer parses), mark_published (an event published but not marked — it will be delivered again), pending_count / leased_count / oldest_pending / blocked_count (a gauge query). | sum by (domain, service, operation) (rate(platform_outbox_errors_total[5m])) > 0. |
| `platform_outbox_dead_letter_operations_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `operation`<br>`operation` ∈ `reprocess`, `discard` | Outbox dead-letter records acted on by an operator call: reprocess (moved back to outbox_events for retry) or discard (permanently deleted). Counts records, not calls. | Audit trail: sum by (domain, service, operation) (increase(platform_outbox_dead_letter_operations_total[1d])). |
| `platform_telemetry_label_overflow_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `label`<br>`label` ∈ `event_type` | A label value the library replaced because it exceeded its cardinality bound: event_type over 128 bytes → `__oversized__`, or a new distinct event_type beyond the per-process limit (default 200) → `__other__`. Counts replacements. Non-zero means a misconfigured or adversarial producer, or a limit set below the service's real number of event types. | sum by (domain, service, label) (rate(platform_telemetry_label_overflow_total[15m])) > 0. |
| `platform_library_info` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | `library`, `library_version` | Always 1. Identifies a platform library and the version a service was built with, for fleet-wide upgrade tracking. | Services still on an old version: count by (library_version) (platform_library_info{library="platform-events"}). |
| `platform_db_queries_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool`, `operation`, `outcome`<br>`operation` ∈ `ALTER`, `ANALYZE`, `BEGIN`, `CALL`, `COMMENT`, `COMMIT`, `COPY`, `CREATE`, `DELETE`, `DISCARD`, `DO`, `DROP`, `END`, `EXPLAIN`, `GRANT`, `INSERT`, `LISTEN`, `LOCK`, `MERGE`, `NOTIFY`, `PREPARE`, `REFRESH`, `RELEASE`, `RESET`, `REVOKE`, `ROLLBACK`, `SAVEPOINT`, `SELECT`, `SET`, `SHOW`, `START`, `TABLE`, `TRUNCATE`, `UNLISTEN`, `UPDATE`, `VACUUM`, `VALUES`, `WITH`, `BATCH`, `other`<br>`outcome` ∈ `success`, `error` | One statement a service executed against PostgreSQL through a pgcommon pool — a query, a SendBatch (operation=BATCH) or a CopyFrom (operation=COPY) — counted when it completes, by outcome. Statements pgcommon issues itself (RLS GUC set_config on acquire, BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, transaction timeouts, savepoints, the PgBouncer wrapping transaction) are excluded unless they fail: a failed COMMIT or GUC injection is a failure of the caller's work. | Error ratio per service: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_db_queries_total{outcome="error"}[5m])) / sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_db_queries_total[5m])). Platform-wide database load: sum by (domain) (rate(platform_db_queries_total[5m])). |
| `platform_db_query_duration_seconds` | platform-pgcommon | histogram (db_query) | proposed | `pool`, `operation`<br>`operation` ∈ `ALTER`, `ANALYZE`, `BEGIN`, `CALL`, `COMMENT`, `COMMIT`, `COPY`, `CREATE`, `DELETE`, `DISCARD`, `DO`, `DROP`, `END`, `EXPLAIN`, `GRANT`, `INSERT`, `LISTEN`, `LOCK`, `MERGE`, `NOTIFY`, `PREPARE`, `REFRESH`, `RELEASE`, `RESET`, `REVOKE`, `ROLLBACK`, `SAVEPOINT`, `SELECT`, `SET`, `SHOW`, `START`, `TABLE`, `TRUNCATE`, `UNLISTEN`, `UPDATE`, `VACUUM`, `VALUES`, `WITH`, `BATCH`, `other` | Client-observed wall time of one statement (query, SendBatch or CopyFrom) against PostgreSQL through a pgcommon pool, from send to result. Library-internal statements (RLS GUC set_config, BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, transaction timeouts, savepoints) are excluded unless they fail: a failed COMMIT or GUC injection is a failure of the caller's work. | p99 per service: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, domain, service) (rate(platform_db_query_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))). Buckets are identical in every service, so cross-service quantiles are valid. |
| `platform_db_pool_acquires_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool`, `outcome`<br>`outcome` ∈ `success`, `error` | One attempt to check a connection out of a pgcommon pool (WithConn, RunInTx and helpers), by outcome; error includes acquire timeouts (context deadline exceeded while waiting) and a closed pool. An attempt abandoned by the caller (context cancelled) is not counted under either outcome; its wait is still recorded in platform_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds. | Acquire failure ratio: sum by (domain, service, pool) (rate(platform_db_pool_acquires_total{outcome="error"}[5m])) / sum by (domain, service, pool) (rate(platform_db_pool_acquires_total[5m])). |
| `platform_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds` | platform-pgcommon | histogram (db_pool_acquire) | proposed | `pool` | Time a caller waited to check a connection out of a pgcommon pool, recorded for every attempt including failures — a saturation signal. | p99 wait per pool: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, domain, service, pool) (rate(platform_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))). |
| `platform_db_slow_queries_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool` | A statement whose wall time exceeded the pool's configured slow-query threshold (Config.SlowQueryThreshold). Counted for every occurrence, independent of log rate limiting. Library-internal statements (RLS GUC set_config, BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, transaction timeouts, savepoints) are excluded. | Thresholds are per-service configuration, so compare trends within a service rather than absolute rates across services. |
| `platform_db_transaction_retries_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool`, `reason`<br>`reason` ∈ `deadlock`, `serialization` | A transaction attempt that failed with a retryable PostgreSQL error and was retried by RunInTxWithRetry*: deadlock (SQLSTATE 40P01) or serialization failure (40001). | Contention board: sum by (domain, service, reason) (rate(platform_db_transaction_retries_total[5m])). |
| `platform_db_transaction_retries_exhausted_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool`, `reason`<br>`reason` ∈ `deadlock`, `serialization` | A RunInTxWithRetry* call that used every attempt and still failed with a retryable error — the operation failed for the caller. | Any sustained non-zero rate is user-visible failure: sum by (domain, service) (increase(platform_db_transaction_retries_exhausted_total[15m])) > 0. |
| `platform_db_pool_connections` | platform-pgcommon | gauge | proposed | `pool`, `state`<br>`state` ∈ `idle`, `acquired`, `constructing` | Connections currently held by a pgcommon pool, by state: idle (available), acquired (checked out), constructing (being dialled). Sampled at scrape time from the pool's statistics. | Utilisation: sum by (domain, service, pool) (platform_db_pool_connections{state="acquired"}) / sum by (domain, service, pool) (platform_db_pool_max_connections). Total = sum over state. |
| `platform_db_pool_max_connections` | platform-pgcommon | gauge | proposed | `pool` | The configured connection limit of a pgcommon pool (Config.MaxConns). | Denominator for utilisation (see platform_db_pool_connections). |
| `platform_db_pool_empty_acquires_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool` | Cumulative acquires that had to wait because every connection was checked out (pool exhausted). A rising rate means the pool is undersized for the service's concurrency. | Saturation: sum by (domain, service, pool) (rate(platform_db_pool_empty_acquires_total[5m])) > 0. |

## Tier 2: domain-shared metrics

| Metric | Owner | Type | Status | Labels | Meaning | Aggregation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `iam_auth_events_total` (iam) | services | counter | proposed | `event_type`, `outcome` | Authentication events (login, logout, token refresh, MFA challenge) observed by an IAM service. | sum by (environment, event_type, outcome) of rate(); identical meaning in every IAM service. |
| `iam_tenant_resolution_total` (iam) | services | counter | proposed | `strategy`, `outcome` | Attempts to resolve the tenant of a request or event. | sum by (environment, strategy, outcome) of rate(). |
| `iam_identity_sync_total` (iam) | services | counter | proposed | `source`, `outcome` | Identity records synchronised from an external identity source. | sum by (environment, source, outcome) of rate(). |
| `iam_realm_operations_total` (iam) | services | counter | proposed | `operation`, `outcome` | Administrative realm operations (create, update, delete, configure). | sum by (environment, operation, outcome) of rate(). |
| `iam_rls_violations_total` (iam) | services | counter | proposed | `violation_type` | Row-level-security violations recorded in the service's rls_violation_log, by violation_type. Fed from a periodic scrape of the log table, not from the request path. | sum by (environment, service, violation_type) of increase(); any increase is a security signal, so alert on > 0 rather than on a ratio. |
| `iam_auth_session_revoke_failed_total` (iam) | services | counter | proposed | `reason`<br>`reason` ∈ `transport`, `http_4xx`, `http_5xx`, `http_other` | Calls to the realm provisioner's RevokeUserSessions that errored or returned non-2xx. The caller fails open (AUTH-8), so every increment is a user session that may outlive its membership. | sum by (environment, service, reason) of rate(); alert on sustained rate > 0. |
| `iam_lifecycle_event_skipped_total` (iam) | services | counter | proposed | `event_type` | Tenant lifecycle events skipped by the recency guard (EVT-14: event time <= the tenant's last applied event time), by event_type. | sum by (environment, service, event_type) of rate(); a sustained rate means out-of-order delivery or a replay. |
| `iam_lifecycle_event_lag_seconds` (iam) | services | histogram (lifecycle_event_lag) | proposed | `event_type` | Seconds from a tenant lifecycle event's envelope time to the moment the consumer applied it, by event_type. Sustained high p99 flags a consumer backlog (SLO-3). | histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, environment, service, event_type) (rate(iam_lifecycle_event_lag_seconds_bucket[5m]))). Includes producer clock skew. |

## Label vocabulary

| Label | Allowed values | Max distinct values | Cardinality | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dependency` | pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` | 50 | bounded by configured dependencies | Downstream dependency (database, broker, HTTP API) by logical name. |
| `domain` | `iam`, `workflow`, `billing`, `tender_management`, `notifications`, `documents`, `bff`, `portal` | - | fixed | Business domain that owns the emitting service. Injected centrally from Config.Domain / OBSERVABILITY_DOMAIN. |
| `environment` | `local`, `dev`, `test`, `staging`, `prod` | - | fixed | Deployment environment. Injected centrally from Config.Environment, else APP_ENV, else ENVIRONMENT (trimmed, lowercased; no aliases, so production is rejected: use prod). Same precedence in every platform library. |
| `error_class` | `success`, `client_error`, `server_error` | - | fixed | Outcome class matching status_class. |
| `event_type` | pattern `^.{1,128}$` | 203 | bounded by the event catalogue and the per-process event_type limit | Event envelope type (<domain>.<entity>.<past-tense-verb>[.v<N>]). Bounded by the emitter: unknown when empty, __oversized__ over 128 bytes, __other__ once the process limit of distinct values (platform-events default 200) is reached. |
| `grpc_code` | `OK`, `Canceled`, `Unknown`, `InvalidArgument`, `DeadlineExceeded`, `NotFound`, `AlreadyExists`, `PermissionDenied`, `ResourceExhausted`, `FailedPrecondition`, `Aborted`, `OutOfRange`, `Unimplemented`, `Internal`, `Unavailable`, `DataLoss`, `Unauthenticated` | - | fixed | gRPC status code name. |
| `grpc_method` | pattern `^(unknown\|/?[A-Za-z0-9_.]+/[A-Za-z0-9_]+)$` | 1000 | bounded by registered services | Full gRPC method name (/package.Service/Method), or unknown. |
| `label` | `event_type` | - | fixed | Name of a label whose values were replaced to bound cardinality. |
| `library` | `platform-gincommon`, `platform-events`, `platform-pgcommon`, `platform-fastapicommon`, `platform-eventcommon`, `platform-pgcommon-py` | - | fixed | Platform library reporting its build, by repository name. Go and Python ports are distinct values because they have separate version streams. |
| `library_version` | pattern `^(devel\|v?[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._+-]{0,63})$` | 5 | one value per deployment | Module version of the library the service was built with (e.g. v1.6.0), devel for an unreleased build. |
| `method` | `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, `CONNECT`, `TRACE`, `OTHER` | - | fixed | HTTP request method. Methods outside the standard set are reported as OTHER. |
| `operation` | pattern `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$` | 100 | bounded enum | Logical operation from the fixed per-metric set declared in the registry entry (e.g. consume, outbox_publish, SQL verbs SELECT/INSERT). |
| `outcome` | `success`, `failure`, `error` | - | fixed | success: completed as intended; failure: rejected for a business reason; error: system or transport fault. Each metric declares the subset it uses. |
| `pool` | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$` | 10 | a handful per service | Database pool name from Config.PoolName (e.g. default, primary, replica), static per deployment. |
| `queue` | pattern `^(unknown\|[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,79})$` | 100 | bounded by configured queues | Queue name: the last path segment of the queue URL (e.g. orders, orders.fifo), never the full URL; unknown when empty. |
| `reason` | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$` | 50 | bounded enum | Failure or routing reason from a fixed per-metric enum, snake_case. Never an error message. |
| `route` | pattern `^(unknown\|/[A-Za-z0-9_./:*~-]*)$` | 1000 | bounded by registered routes | Gin route template (e.g. /api/items/:id), or unknown for unmatched requests. Never the raw URL path. |
| `service` | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$` | - | one value per deployment | Emitting service (e.g. event-consumer). Injected centrally from Config.ServiceName / the library Identity. Same rule as platform-events and platform-pgcommon identities. |
| `source` | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$` | 50 | bounded enum | Origin system of a change or event, snake_case. |
| `state` | `idle`, `acquired`, `constructing` | - | fixed | Connection pool connection state. |
| `status_class` | `2xx`, `4xx`, `5xx` | - | fixed | Response class. HTTP 1xx-3xx and gRPC OK are 2xx; client-side gRPC codes are 4xx; everything else is 5xx. |
| `strategy` | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$` | 20 | bounded enum | Resolution or authentication strategy from a fixed set, snake_case. |
| `topic` | pattern `^(unknown\|[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,255})$` | 100 | bounded by configured topics | Topic name: the last segment of the topic ARN (e.g. iam-events, orders.fifo), never the full ARN; unknown when empty. |
| `transport` | `http`, `grpc` | - | fixed | Inbound transport of the request: http or grpc. |
| `version` | pattern `^[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._+-]{0,63}$` | - | one value per deployment | Build version of the emitting binary (Config.BuildVersion / BUILD_VERSION; unknown when unset). Only on build-info metrics: a per-build label on every series would multiply series on each deploy. |
| `violation_type` | `cross_tenant_access`, `missing_or_invalid_guc`, `missing_primary_email`, `other` | - | fixed | Row-level-security violation class recorded in rls_violation_log by rls_check_tenant() and the service's own checks, snake_case; other for anything outside the set. |

## Prohibited labels

`user_id`, `email`, `tenant_id`, `request_id`, `event_id`, `session_id`, `trace_id`, `span_id`, `correlation_id`, `user`, `username`, `ip`, `client_ip`, `url`, `path`, `query`, `message_id`, `subject`, `actor`, and any label ending in `_id`, `_email`, `_ip`, `_uuid`, `_token`.
